title: Console MVP: consolidate insight cards and trim cost/trace surface for 1st launch
creator: Maya Chen
description: Decision record and implementation plan to reduce the initial Console observability surface for the MVP. We will consolidate multiple fine-grained insight cards into a smaller set of cross-cutting cards and remove non-essential trace and per-route cost views. Goal: deliver a coherent, high-value observability experience within the next release window while deferring lower-impact features to subsequent phases.
background_notes: Original scope included 12 metric cards, per-route cost breakdown, trace waterfall explorer, and session-level token breakdowns.
Recent capacity and telemetry retention trade-offs (storage cost + query perf) mean we cannot reliably meet performance targets for the full surface within the MVP timeline.
Product success metric for MVP: 70% of new Console users find an actionable insight within 2 minutes (measured by guided checklist + survey).
decisions: Consolidate metric cards from 12 to 4: Route Vitals, Cost Trend (aggregated), Error & Retry Overview, Top Latency Contributors.
Remove per-route cost breakdown from MVP; include aggregated route cost share only (top-level % by category).
Defer trace waterfall explorer to Post-MVP; ship trimmed trace quick-links that jump to raw traces (external viewer) instead of an embedded interactive trace UI.
Limit timespan selectors to 1h / 24h / 7d for MVP to simplify backend queries and caching strategies.
Use sampled traces (1%) for trace-related panels to keep storage and query costs acceptable at launch.
Acceptance criteria prioritize clarity of action over completeness: every card must include a recommended next step (e.g., open route, compare model variant, create incident).
tradeoffs_and_rationale: Benefit: shorter delivery path, lower telemetry costs, faster dashboard load times.
Tradeoff: customers lose granular per-route cost visibility on day one; mitigated by clear roadmap and temporary CSV export of raw usage for enterprise customers.
Technical constraint: the current metrics pipeline saturates at peak; reducing cardinality and limiting timespans reduces query load by ~60% per QPS estimate.
UX rationale: early users prioritize signal-to-noise and clear actions; too many small cards dilute attention and increase cognitive load.
acceptance_criteria: Four consolidated cards render within 500ms on a warm cache and 1.5s on cold cache for standard demo accounts.
Top-level Cost Trend shows daily spend and 3-line explanation with a suggested next action (e.g., review model batching policy).
Trace quick-links open sampled raw trace in the linked trace viewer and include a canonical example in the help panel.
Timespan selector exposes only 1h/24h/7d; backend queries fall within SLOs and do not exceed query CPU budget during peak test window (load test results attached).
Product checklist and in-product walkthrough added and validated with 5 internal testers and 3 external beta customers.
Launch release notes and roadmap clearly list deferred items and expected delivery windows for per-route cost and full trace explorer.
